transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (VeraHealth CTO), Liam O'Connor (VeraHealth Platform), Priya Nair (VeraHealth ML)

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, quick agenda — benchmark review vs the baseline provider, tuning notes, and next steps. Ethan will run us through the numbers.
[00:15] Ethan: great, thanks Aisha. Quick caveat — some of the logs came from our staging cluster so timestamps may be a little off and a couple model names are auto-corrected in the export.
[00:30] Ethan: ok first slide, p50/p95/p99 numbers. Baseline provider (we'll call them CloudVendorX here) p95 for the 512-token prompt set was ~420ms, p99 ~980ms. Redwood with default hosted config is p95 ~280ms, p99 ~640ms. These are median-ish across the 2h run.
[01:00] Sofia: hmm that p95 delta is significant, is that with KV cache enabled?
[01:05] Ethan: good question — the numbers I just cited are with prefix caching enabled for repeated prefixes (~30% hit rate in this workload) and a conservative batch window of 20ms. Without caching, Redwood p95 moves to ~360ms. CloudVendorX didn't have prefix cache in their baseline run.
[01:30] Liam: what's the throughput we saw? req/s and tokens/s?
[01:35] Ethan: at 95th percentile concurrent load, baseline hit ~120 req/s and ~60k tokens/s. Redwood at same concurrency hit ~140 req/s and ~72k tokens/s. The throughput advantage is partly due to more aggressive kernel selection and continuous batching in our serving runtime.
[02:00] Priya: are these numbers for hosted or dedicated?
[02:05] Ethan: those numbers are from our hosted POC instances on the same cloud region we asked you to use. For Dedicated, we project similar latency with tighter tail bounds once we tune instance placement and GPU packing.
[02:25] Sofia: curious about variability — p99 still looks in the 600-700ms range; is that spikes due to cold starts or scheduling?
[02:35] Ethan: a mix — some spikes relate to longer context lengths (1k+ tokens), and a few outliers from garbage collection/VM scheduling on the test infra. On Dedicated we avoid noisy neighbors and see p99 tighten by ~15-20%.
[03:00] Aisha: can you call out the exact test parameters so we can reproduce?
[03:05] Ethan: yes — prompt distribution: 60% short (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512), 10% long (512-1,024). Payloads were mixed with 2 temperature settings. Batch window set to 20ms, max batch size 32. KV cache TTL 10 minutes, prefix hit rate ~30%. Model was the open-xxl-v2 (note: transcript may show as open xxl v2).
[03:40] Liam: what about quantization tests? we asked for 4-bit runs last week.
[03:45] Ethan: we ran INT4 quantization on a subset — inference speed improved ~18% throughput and p95 improved ~40ms, but we observed a small quality delta on a handful of hallucination-sensitive prompts — about 2% drop in answer fidelity for those cases. We'll share examples.
[04:10] Priya: that's the tradeoff we expected. Can you run quantized with KV cache enabled? sometimes cache masks quality diffs.
[04:20] Ethan: yes we will, running that in the next test batch.
[04:25] Sofia: cost implications? Redwood hosted vs baseline price per token or per-hour?
[04:30] Aisha: we'll attach a cost sheet — initial rough numbers show Redwood hosted cost per 1M tokens is comparable to baseline but unit economics improve with batching and caching; Dedicated gives the best cost per token at commit levels you talked about. We'll send a Dedicated vs Hosted estimate.
[04:50] Ethan: also noted — batching policy tuning gave us the most leverage. Increasing batch window to 30ms pushed throughput up ~12% but added ~25ms tail on p95 in the short prompt workload. So for latency-sensitive paths short window is better, for throughput-heavy paths longer window can help.
[05:20] Liam: interesting, what about per-request timeouts and KV evictions? we have some tight SLAs.
[05:25] Ethan: we recommend p50-targeted routes for interactive UI and p95-targeted for async pipelines. For KV evictions, TTL and cache sizing you can tune per route; we'll provide recommended defaults. Also note our routing layer can fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency rises, preserving availability but at slightly different quality.
[06:00] Priya: any notes on security/compliance from the POC infra? we need SOC2 + SSO for the final pilot.
[06:08] Aisha: yes we've already shared SOC 2 Type II attestation and our SSO integrations (SAML). For Private/VPC there's also KMS/HSM options and audit logs — we'll attach the security pack again.
[06:25] Sofia: good. Back to benchmarks — were there any mem/copy issues with large context? we saw some OOMs in our baseline runs.
[06:35] Ethan: Redwood runtime uses KV-sharding and streaming kv loads so we saw fewer OOMs; the only outliers were when a single request hit 2k+ tokens plus aggressive batch packing. We cap batch packing by total tokens to avoid that.
[07:05] Aisha: going forward what's the experiment plan? Ethan?
[07:10] Ethan: next batch: 1) run INT4 quantized tests with KV cache on; 2) run a 24h stress run at sustained 150 req/s to see tail behavior and GC patterns; 3) run dedicated-sim estimates (simulate no noisy neighbor). We'll post all logs and the annotated CSV.
[07:30] Priya: can you also include the exact seed prompts and failure-case examples we flagged last week?
[07:35] Ethan: yes, add those to the artifact.
[07:40] Sofia: timeline — we'd like to have the 24h run results by next Tuesday, that fits our evaluation window. Procurement is aiming for decision by end of month but needs cost + security docs.
[07:55] Aisha: action items we'll track in the repo and I'll send the follow-up with attachments and calendar invite. Anything else?
[08:05] Liam: one quick question — when you say "continuous batching" can that be disabled per-route? we have one latency-critical route.
[08:12] Ethan: yes per-route overrides exist — you can set batch window to 0 for single-request immediate execution. Also can pin specific model versions per route.
[08:25] Priya: were the baseline runs run with quantization? baseline said they used fp16 only. So that might explain part of the gap.
[08:32] Ethan: correct, CloudVendorX baseline used fp16; our quantized runs are additional and show the best tradeoffs. We'll make sure to label that in the sheet.
[08:45] Aisha: recap: Redwood to share annotated benchmark CSV, cost estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated, run INT4+KV tests, run 24h stress test at 150 req/s, VeraHealth to provide additional failure prompts and confirm procurement timeline. We'll reconvene same time next week.
[09:05] Sofia: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:10] Aisha: thanks team, talk soon.

Notes: transcription contains a few auto-corrections (Redwood sometimes appears as RedWood, KV cache transcribed as KV cash), timestamps are approximate. References: benchmark spreadsheet link (shared in chat), security packet link (shared), dedicated cost estimate (to follow).
